headline: Would have canceled a federal rule that moved the northern long-eared bat from "threatened" to "endangered" under the Endangered Species Act.
what_it_does: This resolution would have used the Congressional Review Act to cancel a U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service rule published on November 30, 2022. That rule changed the northern long-eared bat's status from threatened to endangered. It also ended a special rule written just for the bat that applied only while it was listed as threatened. Congress passed the resolution, but the President vetoed it, and the Senate failed to override the veto on September 28, 2023.

who_it_affects.group: Landowners, builders, loggers, energy companies, and others whose work may affect bat habitat
who_it_affects.how: The bat would have kept its threatened status and its special rule, instead of falling under the stricter protections that come with an endangered listing.

who_it_affects.group: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
who_it_affects.how: The agency's rule would have been canceled, and under the Congressional Review Act it generally could not issue a substantially similar rule without new approval from Congress.
The species would have stayed listed as threatened rather than endangered under federal law.
